column1: # FIXTURE exempt table. The row is a bare `*`, written by an author who read the column as a
# glob and meant "the legacy scripts, for now". It is not a glob. `*` is the private sentinel
# scandir_prefixes mints for `scandir: .`, and covers() used to honour it from EITHER side, so
# this one row matched a tracked script in Pass 1 and then exempted every script in Pass 2 —
# an exit 0 over a repository with an unscanned directory in it. THE PREVIOUS VERSION OF THE
# SCRIPT ADMITS THIS FIXTURE; this is the case that tells the two versions apart. The refusal
# it must produce is the one Pass 2 gives for unscanned/run.sh, not merely any exit 1: if the
# sentinel guard in is_under regressed, the row would still be refused by Pass 1 as a prefix
# matching no tracked file, and the case would go green over a broken guard.
